newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slip 0.75 pct on lack of cash.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slip 0.75 pct on lack of cash.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued to slide in quiet selling on Tuesday amid a lack of fresh cash entry after recent sharp gains, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 700.17 points, or 0.75 percent lower at 93,217.11, bringing two-day falls to 1.26 percent since Friday's all-time high closing of 94,407.22.
Trade volume firmed to 14.36 trillion lira from Monday's 12.20 trillion.
"There is no cash entry to the market. An easing towards 91,000 levels or sideways trade is seen possible The market may test 93,000 support tomorrow," said Okan Alpay from Interbank.
The index had leapt 2.89 percent last week after a 5.49 percent surge the previous week and hit nine record closes in the last two weeks.

Of the 231 shares traded, 89 declined, 75 advanced and 67 closed stable. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI eased 0.92 percent to 97,817.14 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF edged 0.36 percent lower to 91,577.48.

Actives were led by Ihlas Holding, up 750 lira at 15,500, airport ground handling firm Celebi, down 1,500 lira at 38,500, supermarket chain Tansas, up 750 lira at 23,750 and steel rope producer Celik Halat, up 100 lira at 5,600.
They made up 18.2 percent of the total volume.
